subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should Slack setup/docs resolve this by adding latency-aware HTTP Request URL guidance, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists, but stronger setup steering or default changes would alter operator expectations and deployment requirements, so maintainer intent is required.

options.title: Document HTTP Latency Guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the local/private default and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change Setup Or Defaults
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup/default change toward HTTP mode with explicit upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept Current Transport Guidance
options.body: Close only after maintainers decide the current deployment-shape table is enough and no latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP Latency Guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the local/private default and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the measurements, authored the partial Slack fixes, and named the remaining HTTP-guidance scope.
